prompt: We're building a content management system as a side project — blog posts, media metadata, user-generated content with varying schemas per content type. What database would work well?
output:
For a side project CMS, **PostgreSQL with JSONB** is the strongest fit — and you already know it well from Helios, so there's no new infra to learn or operate.

**Schema approach:**

```sql
-- Structured content (blog posts)
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  slug TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  body TEXT,
  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  metadata JSONB  -- tags, SEO fields, etc.
);

-- Flexible UGC / varying schemas per type
CREATE TABLE content_items (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,         -- 'video', 'gallery', 'review', etc.
  data JSONB NOT NULL,        -- schema varies by type
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON content_items USING gin(data);  -- fast JSON queries
```

**Why this works well:**

- JSONB handles per-content-type schema variance without fighting the DB
- `tsvector` / `to_tsvector` gives you full-text search on post bodies for free
- GIN index on JSONB makes querying nested metadata fast
- Flyway (which you already use) handles migrations cleanly
- No separate infra — runs alongside your existing Postgres or a cheap managed instance (Supabase free tier, Railway, Render)

**One trade-off to know:** deeply nested or frequently mutating JSONB gets messy over time. If a content type stabilizes (e.g., media always has the same 10 fields), migrate it to proper columns. Start flexible, tighten as schemas stabilize.

For a low-traffic side project, SQLite + [Litestream](https://litestream.io) for streaming backup is also worth considering — zero managed DB cost, same SQL skills, trivially simple ops.
